htmlTitle: How many square metres can you afford? — housing affordability in Europe and the United States
metaDescription: Type your net income and see how many square metres you could buy or rent in 8,489 European municipalities: 22 million listings from the ESPON HOUSE4ALL dataset behind the 2026 TU Wien study. Plus 3,141 US counties measured in years of income and rent share, because American public data does not publish floor area at all.
ogDescription: Your income, 11,630 places in Europe and the United States: how many square metres a third of it buys or rents, built from open data and honest about what does not compare.
imageAlt: Two maps side by side, Europe by municipality and the United States by county, dotted in five shades from light to dark, dark where a third of the average income buys the least space
title: How many square metres can you afford?
ldDescription: An interactive calculator and map of housing affordability: net income in, affordable square metres out, for 8,489 municipalities and 1,251 NUTS 3 regions in 31 European countries (ESPON HOUSE4ALL, the dataset behind Sielker and Banabak 2026, Journal of Maps); and years of income and rent share for 3,141 United States counties from the American Community Survey 2020-2024, where floor area is not published and square metres cannot be computed.
ldDatasetName: Housing affordability by European municipality and US county, 2024–2026
ldDatasetDescription: Per-municipality (LAU) sale price and rent per square metre, mean equivalised disposable income 2024, national mortgage rate and the square metres a third of the local mean income buys on a 30-year mortgage or rents, for 89,601 municipalities in 34 European countries, extracted from the public ESPON HOUSE4ALL feature service (TU Wien, InAtlas, MCRIT) on 14 September 2026; and per-county median home value, median household income, median gross rent and population from the US Census Bureau American Community Survey five-year estimates 2020-2024, with the Freddie Mac 30-year fixed rate for 2024, for 3,141 US counties. No floor area is published for US counties, so square metres are not computed there.
